title: Config Deploy Watchtower: Automated Safe-Failover & Reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a "watchtower" service for config deployments that automatically detects unsafe changes to batching/caching and other runtime knobs, applies guarded rollouts, and performs automatic safe rollback and state reconciliation when guardrails are breached. This ticket covers the core orchestration and policy enforcement: triggers (signal definition), guardrail checks (safety predicates), reconcile loop (idempotent state), and safe-apply/rollback flows. Goal: reduce manual intervention for config-induced regressions and cut mean-time-to-recovery for unsafe config changes to < 5 minutes for P1 incidents.
problem_statement: Config-only changes (batch size, cache TTLs, KV cache modes, quantization toggles) have caused intermittent cost regressions and latency spikes when misapplied at scale. Current process is manual rollback or database patching which delays mitigation and causes customer impact. We need an automated, auditable mechanism that can detect regressions, stop rollouts, rollback to last-known-good state, and reconcile drift between desired config and actual runtime state.
design_summary:
- Triggers: metric-based and event-based triggers. Primary metrics: 99p latency, SLO error rate, tokens-per-second cost delta, GPU utilization delta, and e2e ingestion QPS. Secondary signals: schema failures, model mismatch, and rollout health checks.
- Guardrails: threshold windows with hysteresis, minimum sample sizes, rollout throttling (max concurrent variants), and time-of-day/region exemptions.
- Safe apply: staged canary -> progressively increased cohorts -> automated pause points with evaluation windows.
- Rollback: deterministic state revert using immutable config versions with tombstones; rollback conditions are either threshold breaches or system errors during apply.
- Reconciliation: leader-driven loop that compares desired config store (git-backed or KV-store) with actual server-side config; corrective apply is idempotent and accompanied by a dry-run verification step.
- Observability & audit: every apply/rollback emits structured events to the console, audit log with actor, commit hash, and diagnostics snapshot (metrics & recent traces).
- Safety-first UX: explicit "force-apply" required for emergency overrides, with additional approval audit path.
acceptance_criteria: Define at least 5 metric-based triggers and document threshold formulas
Implement a canary rollout controller with throttles and pause windows
Implement automatic rollback when 99p latency increases > 30% over baseline for a 3-minute sustained window
Reconciliation loop runs every 30s and corrects drift within 2 minutes for >90% of cases
Emit structured audit events and link to Console rollout dashboard for every config change
notes_and_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with runtime, ops, and observability. Agreed to use existing config-store service (git-backed) and extend it with versioned snapshots.
2026-03-11: Spike completed for metric collectors — added tokens-per-sec and cost-delta metrics to the metrics pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/3412).
2026-03-12: Chose hysteresis window approach for guardrails to avoid flapping during transient spikes. Trade-off: slightly slower reaction time for noise reduction.

2026-03-13: Implemented canary controller prototype (branch: feat/rollout-watchtower). Running unit tests for throttling logic. TODO: add integration test against runtime simulator that replays high-QPS traces.

2026-03-14: Design review feedback from PM (Asha Patel) — request to add a cost-surge detection trigger and a soft-warning stage before a full rollback. Action: add configurable soft-warning window that emits paged alerts but does not auto-rollback for first occurrence.

Next steps: finish reconciliation leader election, add emergency override flow, and write e2e test harness that simulates cache misconfiguration scenarios (latency spike, OOM, and token cost increase).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False-positive rollbacks during noisy traffic — mitigation: sample-size checks and hysteresis windows
Risk: Reconciliation causing config churn if leader flaps — mitigation: leader lease + backoff + idempotent applies
Risk: Partial rollout left in inconsistent state across regions — mitigation: region-aware cohorts and per-region rollback streams
Risk: Increased load from reconciliation loop — mitigation: exponential backoff + batching reconciliation diffs
testing_plan: Unit tests for guardrail predicates and canary throttles
Integration test using runtime simulator with replayed traces (QA lab)
Chaos test: force network partition during apply and verify rollback correctness
Load test: run reconciliation loop under high config-change volume and assert CPU < 5% extra per node
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged deploy to staging cluster with synthetic traffic (2 weeks)
Stage 2: enable in production on a small non-critical customer cohort (10%) and monitor for 72h
Stage 3: progressive enable across regions with monitoring + ops runbook (if rollbacks > 1 in 24h, pause rollout)
Stage 4: GA and document in Console release notes
owner_notes: Make reconciliation idempotent and avoid two-phase commits across thousands of worker processes. Prioritize observability hooks so on-call can triage rollbacks quickly. Coordinate with SRE for runbook and on-call paging thresholds.
